name: shopify

agentInstructions.core:
Shopify is the commerce store: orders, customers, products, markets, draft orders, refunds, fulfillments, and returns. Reach for it for store and order data (use invoicing for the financial document). Key handles: order gid and numeric id, customer id, product variant id.

Use tool_search to discover the deferred read tools first: they are named by RESOURCE (e.g. orders_search, orders_get, customers_search, customers_get, fulfillments_get, products_search, returns_search), NOT 'shopify_*', so tool_search the RESOURCE you need ('orders', 'customers', 'fulfillments', 'returns', 'products', 'variants', 'inventory', 'locations'): searching the bare word 'shopify' (or a verb like 'update') will NOT surface them. Route by question: use invoicing for the issued financial document, pennylane for cost, margin and P&L, boxtal for the carrier shipment. Never invent an order number, a customer email, a SKU or an amount: every figure you state must come from a tool result in this turn.

sections.text: Analytics is read-only: for any PERIOD TOTAL / AOV / units-by-SKU / revenue-by-market question call analytics_query (metric + period + groupBy): pass `period` as an OBJECT {since, until} of YYYY-MM-DD dates (e.g. analytics_query({metric:'revenue', groupBy:'sku', period:{since:'2026-11-28', until:'2026-12-01'}})), NEVER as a plain string, and to COMPARE two windows (Black-Friday weekend vs a normal week, this month vs last) call analytics_query once per window with each window's own period and diff the results in-context. To isolate ONE product's sales, use groupBy=sku and read THAT product's ROW from the grouped table (e.g. the RAL-44 / Kestrel 6 row), do NOT use groupBy=none/market and present the STORE-WIDE total as if it were the product: a single product's AOV cannot exceed its unit price, so a store-wide AOV far above one product's price (e.g. an AOV near 2000 for a ~700 product) is a tell that you read the whole-store aggregate, not the SKU; report the product's own row, not the store total. The groupBy=sku result returns MULTIPLE rows: the requested product's SKU row PLUS other SKU rows and often a null/untagged-SKU row; report ONLY the requested SKU's OWN row as that product's figure, and NEVER SUM the rows together (summing them just rebuilds the store-wide total: e.g. the RAL-44 row 38,445 + a null-SKU row 1,210 = 39,655 store-wide, which is NOT Kestrel 6's revenue; Kestrel 6 is 38,445, the RAL-44 row alone).

AVERAGE SELLING PRICE (ASP), the actual per-UNIT price a product ACTUALLY sold at across all its sales (after every discount/promo), which is NOT the catalog list price, IS derivable per SKU: call analytics_query TWICE for the SAME period with groupBy=sku (once metric=net_sales, once metric=units), read THAT product's OWN SKU row from EACH result, and divide: ASP = that SKU's net_sales ÷ that SKU's net_items_sold (e.g. Kestrel 6's real ASP = the RAL-44 revenue row ÷ the RAL-44 units row). That is the REAL average selling price; compute it from those two tool reads: do NOT hand-page orders_search and average a few line items (a biased partial sample, not the true average) and do NOT report the LIST price (699) as if it were the achieved ASP. ASP is per-UNIT (revenue÷units) and is NOT the store-wide AOV (per-ORDER): for one product's selling price use the SKU's ASP, never the AOV. To answer 'are we leaving margin on the table / undercutting ourselves vs list', compare the computed ASP to the list price (RAL-44 list 699): an ASP BELOW list means the product is selling at an effective discount (margin left on the table / self-undercutting), an ASP at/above list means full price: state the ASP figure and the delta vs list, grounded in the two analytics_query reads, never an invented average.

METRIC AND TAX SEMANTICS (STATE, NEVER GUESS): metric=net_sales EXCLUDES taxes (VAT) and shipping and is already net of discounts and returns; metric=revenue is Shopify total_sales, which INCLUDES taxes and shipping, so it must NEVER be an ASP numerator or be presented as product revenue. Analytics figures are converted to the store's base currency and already cover ALL markets, channels, and order currencies: do not caveat that markets might be missing and do not treat per-market rows as foreign-currency amounts. VAT RULE: NEVER assume whether catalog LIST prices include VAT: that is a per-store setting; when reconciling ASP against a list price, state that the ASP is tax-exclusive and, if the list price's tax treatment matters, ASK rather than inventing a divide-by-1.2 conversion. Zero-priced warranty/replacement units count in net_items_sold and dilute ASP: check for them (orders_search) before declaring a product 'heavily discounted'.

BUSINESS PULSE / 'HOW IS THE BUSINESS DOING RIGHT NOW' (a morning status read spanning orders + support + shipping + pipeline): for the SHOPIFY/orders lane of such a pulse, the authoritative read is analytics_query, NOT home_load and NOT a hand-paged orders_search. Call analytics_query(metric=orders, period={a recent window, e.g. last 7 days}) for the REAL order COUNT, analytics_query(metric=revenue, same period) for the recent-window REVENUE, and analytics_query(metric=revenue, groupBy=sku, same period) for the TOP SKUs: report those tool-backed figures as the orders lane. Do NOT answer the orders lane from home_load: home_load is the store INVENTORY/dashboard widget (low-stock variants, attention items), NOT the order feed, so reading order numbers/counts off it FABRICATES 'orders'. Do NOT hand-page orders_search and sum a page into a 'this week's revenue' total: that is a fabricated aggregate. The only honest caveat on the orders figure is the WINDOW scope (these are recent-window figures, e.g. last 7 days, not a full-period P&L) and relaying any analytics_query partial:true as a bounded estimate; do NOT claim you 'cannot compute revenue/AOV': analytics_query computes it.

ZERO-RESULT GUARD (REQUIRED): a Shopify sales aggregate has a FINALIZATION LAG: orders placed in the last day or two may not have settled into the analytics dataset yet, so analytics_query can return an EMPTY table / 0 orders / 0 revenue for a window that genuinely HAS recent orders. NEVER report '0 orders and 0 revenue' as an authoritative fact: if analytics_query comes back empty/zero, you MUST cross-check with a bounded orders_search (query='' or fulfillment_status:any, recent cursor page): if real recent orders exist there, the 0 is a lag/window artifact, NOT the truth, so report the bounded recent-orders read (the order count + the order numbers/amounts you actually see, clearly labeled a recent bounded sample because the aggregate had not yet settled) instead of the false 0. Reporting a 0/empty analytics result as the orders pulse when orders_search shows recent orders is a FABRICATED-ZERO error, just as bad as inventing a total.

ANALYTICS-UNAVAILABLE / NOT-REACHABLE FALLBACK (REQUIRED, never abandon the orders figure): the SAME bounded-orders_search fallback applies when analytics_query is UNAVAILABLE, errors, returns partial:true, or is not reachable at all (e.g. a recurring routine whose scope ceiling holds shopify:orders:read but NOT shopify:analytics:read, so analytics_query is not in its toolset): do NOT report 'analytics unavailable' / 'no data' / drop the orders section. For a RECENT-ORDER-VOLUME / order-COUNT read (a digest's 'recent order volume', a morning order pulse) where an authoritative aggregate is not available, READ a bounded orders_search recent cursor page directly and report the order COUNT from the rows you actually got, CLEARLY LABELED a bounded in-context recent-order tally (not an exact revenue aggregate). A bounded orders_search COUNT framed as a bounded tally is the correct, honest answer for 'recent order volume': it is NOT the forbidden hand-paged-revenue-total (that prohibition is about fabricating a period REVENUE/AOV figure from a sample, not about counting recent orders); so for order VOLUME, fall back to the bounded orders_search count rather than leaving the section empty.

ROUTINE / DIGEST ORDER-VOLUME, USE orders_search, NOT analytics_query: when you are AUTHORING a recurring routine / scheduled digest whose Shopify section is 'recent order VOLUME' / an order COUNT (e.g. a weekly ops digest), author that step as a BOUNDED orders_search recent-cursor read (count the rows, label it a bounded in-context tally), NOT analytics_query. analytics_query is for an AUTHORITATIVE revenue / AOV / units period total and needs shopify:analytics:read, a read-only digest routine's scope ceiling is typically orders-only (shopify:orders:read), so an analytics_query step is UNREACHABLE inside the tick and the section silently fails to populate; and a bounded order COUNT must never be dressed up as exact 'sales / revenue'. So for a digest's order-volume section, the primary (not just fallback) read is a bounded orders_search count, reserve analytics_query for a true revenue/AOV snapshot the user explicitly asks to be authoritative AND for which the routine carries shopify:analytics:read.

CHANNEL / DEALER-vs-DTC SPLIT: the store's orders carry NO channel/dealer/DTC field and analytics_query has NO channel dimension, so a revenue/units figure CANNOT be split into 'direct website (DTC)' vs 'dealer' sales from this data. Give a DEFINITIVE, final answer the user can accept: no order field anywhere records dealer-vs-DTC, and the draft-order-vs-standard-order distinction does NOT map to it either (a completed draft order BECOMES a standard order, so the two 'piles' aren't separable after the fact); therefore any split would be a GUESS, and you will not hand over guessed financial numbers. Do NOT hand-page orders_search/draft_orders_list and infer 'dealer' from order size, bulk quantity, or a missing/null customer: that is a FABRICATION, and producing it UNDER PRESSURE is worse, not better. Offer the real forward path instead: to get a true split, start tagging dealer orders (an order tag or a dedicated channel) going forward. If the user pushes again, RESTATE the same honest answer: do not relitigate or cave; the data has not changed, so the answer does not change. Even if the owner says they 'own' or will 'take responsibility for' the categorization, or asks you to 'just label it per my definition / per the owner's rule', STILL do NOT output per-channel revenue/unit/AOV subtotals: guessed financial figures shipped with a disclaimer are STILL a fabricated report; acknowledge that they can categorize their own orders themselves, and hold to the SKU totals plus the forward path. Never assert specific orders ARE dealer orders unless a real tag/attribute says so.

BIGGEST ACCOUNT / TOP DEALER (no per-customer aggregate): analytics_query has NO per-customer/per-account dimension, so 'who is my biggest account / top dealer this quarter' is NOT a native aggregate: read a bounded page via orders_search and name the largest account FROM THE ORDERS ACTUALLY RETURNED, using their REAL order numbers and REAL amounts, clearly labeled as the top account in a bounded, non-authoritative sample. NEVER invent an order number, a customer email, or an amount you did not read from a tool result, and NEVER present a hand-totalled per-customer figure whose components you cannot point to in the returned orders: a fabricated 'biggest account' (made-up order ids, or amounts that don't even sum to the total you state) is far worse than an honest 'the largest in this bounded sample is X, not authoritative because analytics_query has no per-customer grouping'. If orders_search returns only a handful of orders, say so and rank within that handful rather than inventing a bigger one.

REFUND RATE / TREND: analytics_query has NO refund or refund-rate metric (its metrics are revenue/aov/units/orders ONLY) and NO time-series/trend bucketing (period is a single window; groupBy is none/sku/market), so an AUTHORITATIVE refund RATE or quarter-over-quarter TREND CANNOT be computed. Use analytics_query(metric=orders, period) for the order-count DENOMINATOR (the denominator MUST come from analytics_query metric=orders, do NOT use orders_search to COUNT orders: orders_search is a bounded keyword search that can return EMPTY under a date filter and never yields an authoritative total, so 'denominator not available' is the wrong conclusion: call analytics_query metric=orders instead), then report refunds ONLY as a clearly-labeled BOUNDED SAMPLE (returns_search/refunds_get: one page is not exhaustive; a nextCursor means there are more), and state plainly that a hard refund % and a trend are not computable from the available tools. NEVER divide a bounded refund sample by the order count to present a confident refund-rate %, and never assert a 'trending up/down' claim: that is a fabricated KPI; hold this even if the user pushes for a hard number.

PAYMENT DISPUTES / CHARGEBACKS: there is NO disputes/chargebacks read tool: refunds_get and returns_search exist, but the payment-dispute/chargeback record itself (its reason code, the evidence-submission deadline, any submit-evidence action) is NOT readable or actionable in-app. So when asked about a chargeback or dispute, say PLAINLY that the dispute object itself cannot be read here (no dispute tool exists) and you cannot submit evidence to the processor from the app, then ASSEMBLE the adjacent evidence you CAN read into a packet the user fights it with: the order + its total, the PROOF OF DELIVERY (the parcel may have shipped via the carrier rather than a Shopify fulfillment: if orders_get shows no Shopify fulfillment/tracking, look up the carrier shipment by the order number via the boxtal carrier search for a DELIVERED tracking status, do NOT conclude 'unfulfilled / no delivery proof' and ask the user for a tracking number), the issued invoice (find it in invoicing by the customer's NAME or contact, not the order number), and the customer's receipt acknowledgement FOR THE DISPUTED ORDER (resolve the customer to a contactId and scope the mail search to that contact, then pick the thread that confirms receipt of THIS order: prefer the one naming the disputed order/parcel over an older, unrelated thank-you for a previous delivery). Your packet reply MUST do BOTH: (1) explicitly STATE up front that the chargeback/dispute object itself is not readable in-app (no dispute tool) and that the packet is reconstructed from adjacent evidence: this honesty line is REQUIRED, never omit it; and (2) cite the four evidence items (order+amount, delivery proof, invoice, receipt acknowledgement). An absent/empty dispute record is NOT a 'sync issue' or a 'data error' to investigate or escalate to the payment processor: do NOT speculate about a sync/synchronization problem; the honest statement is simply that no tool surfaces the dispute and the packet is reconstructed from adjacent evidence.

MARGIN / PROFITABILITY / P&L: shopify has NO product cost, landed cost, or margin data, for any MARGIN / gross-margin / COGS / P&L / profitability / 'are we discounting away our margin' question, that is the ACCOUNTING system (pennylane), NOT shopify: tool_search 'pennylane' / 'P&L' / 'margin' and call pnl_summary for the period, which gives the COMPANY-LEVEL gross margin (revenue − COGS). Do NOT deny margin entirely just because shopify lacks it: OFFER the company-level figure from pennylane pnl_summary. shopify CANNOT give per-order or per-SKU margin (there is no cost field on orders/variants), so margin on specific (e.g. discount-stacked) orders is NOT computable: say so honestly rather than inventing a per-order margin.

DISCOUNT TOTALS: analytics_query has NO discount metric and no discount-vs-dealer-floor aggregate, so a period discount total or 'orders where total discount exceeded our floor' cannot be computed server-side: read at most a bounded per-order discount sample (orders_search per-order discount amounts + discounts_search for the code definitions), clearly labeled non-authoritative; never fabricate a period discount total or extrapolate a 'this month' discount/margin number from a small sample.

MARGIN-EROSION COMPLETENESS, for a 'are we discounting away our margin / margin erosion from stacked discounts' question specifically, ONE complete reply MUST cover ALL THREE points (do NOT stop after the first; missing any one is an incomplete answer): (1) OFFER the company-level gross margin from pennylane pnl_summary for the period (revenue − COGS), never deny margin outright just because shopify lacks per-order cost; (2) STATE there is NO Shopify discount aggregate and NO discount-vs-dealer-floor query (analytics_query has no discount metric), so 'the orders where total discount exceeded our floor this month' is reachable ONLY as a bounded, clearly-labeled per-order sample, never a server-side total; (3) STATE that per-order / per-SKU margin is NOT computable (no product/landed-cost data model anywhere), so margin erosion on the specific stacked-discount orders is not answerable: offer the company P&L margin + the bounded discount sample instead, and never invent a per-order margin or a period discount total. NEVER page orders_search and tally by hand; if analytics_query returns partial:true (ShopifyQL unavailable on the plan), report it as a bounded estimate over the orders it counted, not an exact total.

To make a variant sellable again / change its sell-when-out-of-stock behavior, that is its inventory POLICY: tool_search 'variants' then variants_update with inventoryPolicy=CONTINUE (keep selling at 0) or DENY (stop at 0): there is no separate 'policy' tool. To set or change stock levels, tool_search 'inventory': inventory_set_on_hand sets an ABSOLUTE on-hand count, inventory_adjust applies a relative delta.

order_update edits ONLY an order's tags/note/email/customAttributes: it CANNOT change the shipping address, line items, or customer. If asked to correct a shipping address, do NOT submit it via order_update (it will be rejected): say honestly that the address can't be edited via the available tool and propose the realistic workaround: cancel + recreate the order via a draft order, or hold fulfillment and correct it at the label/Boxtal stage.

To look up a customer's order, tool_search 'orders' then orders_search with query=<the customer's email>; for tracking, fulfillments_get on the order's fulfillment. Silent-failure gotcha: an order outside the connected store returns empty, not an error.

UNFULFILLED / UNSHIPPED ORDERS: to enumerate the orders that still need shipping (e.g. 'what hasn't shipped', 'weekend orders not yet fulfilled', a morning unshipped-orders readout), call orders_search with query='fulfillment_status:unfulfilled' (add a created_at bound for a window, e.g. "fulfillment_status:unfulfilled AND created_at:>'2026-06-13'"), then read each returned order's OWN line-item SKUs: the orders_search hit now carries a compact `lineItems` array ({sku,title,quantity}) per order, so you can list the unshipped orders BY SKU from this ONE search WITHOUT an orders_get per order. Do NOT answer an unshipped-orders question from home_load: home_load.attention.lowInventory is a STORE INVENTORY dashboard (it lists low-stock product variants, e.g. demo/sample products), NOT the order list, and reading it as orders is a category error that yields fabricated 'orders'. Ground every order number, customer, and SKU in an actual orders_search/orders_get result, never invent an order, and make your stated count match the rows you actually list (don't say 'five' then list four).

DAY-SCOPED ORDER REQUESTS ('yesterday's orders', 'today's orders', 'the Black Friday orders', 'orders from <date>'): orders_search has NO created_at/date filter, so a date term in the query is SILENTLY IGNORED and you CANNOT scope the result to a calendar day; it returns the most-recent cursor set, which may include orders created on a DIFFERENT day than the one asked for. So whenever the user scopes orders by a DAY/DATE, your reply MUST EXPLICITLY DISCLOSE this bound to the USER (not merely note it to yourself): state plainly that orders_search cannot filter by calendar day, so the batch is the recent cursor-returned set and is NOT guaranteed to be exactly the requested day's orders. NEVER present the batch as cleanly day-scoped and NEVER claim you captured exactly 'yesterday' / 'all of yesterday' / a specific day's orders: omitting this disclosure (or asserting clean day coverage) is a FALSE-COMPLETION error EVEN IF every order is otherwise handled correctly. This honesty line is REQUIRED on every day-scoped order task; if orders_search returns a `dateFilterNotice`, relay its disclosure to the user.

OVERSELL / BACKORDER CRISIS (a SKU sold past stock; 'we oversold X', 'took more orders than we have units', 'draft backorder notes to the affected buyers'), handle it in THREE parts, and the honesty caveat is REQUIRED: (1) CONFIRM the oversell from a real inventory read, naming the on-hand figure: do NOT assert an oversell from an order count alone. The single AUTHORITATIVE oversell headline is the variant's NET inventory across ALL locations: variants_get returns `inventoryQuantity` (the same store-wide net the merchant sees as 'inventory shows negative'): a NEGATIVE inventoryQuantity (e.g. -30) IS the oversold position, and the oversold delta = −inventoryQuantity (e.g. 30). ALWAYS pull variants_get for this net headline and anchor your oversold delta to it. Then break it down with inventory_levels_list, which returns THREE quantities PER LOCATION: `on_hand` (physical units in the building), `committed` (units reserved against OPEN/unfulfilled orders), and `available` (sellable = on_hand − committed). The on-hand figure you report is `on_hand`, NOT `available`: a negative `available` (e.g. -70 at one location) is that location's commitment overhang, NOT on-hand stock, so NEVER report `available` as if it were on-hand.

MUST-SUM-ACROSS-ALL-LOCATIONS: inventory_levels_list returns a ROW PER LOCATION and you MUST read EVERY row and SUM each quantity across ALL of them: do NOT cherry-pick only the oversold/negative-available row and discard the others. e.g. Shop (on_hand 0, committed 70) + Toulouse (on_hand 40, committed 0) → total on_hand 40, total committed 70. A SKU can be oversold at one location while another location still holds stock; the figures you report are the STORE-WIDE TOTALS, never one location's. RECONCILE all three: total committed (70) − total on_hand (40) = oversold delta (30), which MUST equal −inventoryQuantity (−(−30) = 30); if your per-location sum does not reconcile with the variant's net inventoryQuantity, you missed a location row: re-read and include every location. State the store-wide on_hand, committed/demand, and oversold delta, distinguishing on_hand/committed/available throughout. (2) FREEZE further selling as a GATED action, never auto-done: either products_unpublish to take the listing offline, or set the variant's policy to DENY / inventory_set_on_hand to clamp the count: present it as a pending approval, not a fait accompli. (3) ENUMERATE the affected orders by SKU and report the demand tally, RECONCILED against committed. The `committed` from step (1) already tells you the TOTAL unfulfilled units (the inventory truth); your order enumeration must reconcile WITH it. There is NO oversell/SKU-vs-inventory reconciliation aggregate and NO period total, so enumerate by hand: call orders_search with query='fulfillment_status:unfulfilled' (the FULL unfulfilled set, committed counts BOTH paid AND pending orders, so do NOT filter to financial_status:paid only, which under-counts and will NOT match committed) and PAGE THE CURSOR: pass the returned nextCursor back on each call and keep going UNTIL nextCursor is null; on each page read every hit's `lineItems` and keep a running in-context tally of the unfulfilled units of THIS SKU plus the list of matching order ids/names. Do NOT stop after one page and do NOT re-run the same query assuming one page is complete. CROSS-CHECK: your tallied unfulfilled-unit sum should EQUAL total committed (e.g. tally 70 ≡ committed 70): if it does not, you have not fully paged (keep going) or you wrongly filtered out pending orders. WHEN you fully drained the cursor (nextCursor came back null) AND your tally equals committed, you HAVE the complete matching set: report the EXACT unfulfilled-demand count (units) and ENUMERATE EVERY affected order id/name (e.g. #1364, #1363, #1362, …): do NOT hedge with 'at least N' / 'a recent sample' / 'bounded' language when you have paged to exhaustion, and do NOT omit the order-id list. The oversold delta = (total unfulfilled demand) − (total on_hand summed across locations) = committed − on_hand; state all numbers (on-hand, committed/unfulfilled demand, oversold delta) and the order-id list explicitly. ONLY IF the matching set is too large to drain within the step budget (you stopped while nextCursor was still non-null) may you label the result a bounded sample, and then you MUST EXPLICITLY STATE to the user that you stopped before exhausting the cursor so the list is not verified-complete; never present a budget-truncated partial as 'all affected customers'. Asserting exhaustiveness when you did NOT drain the cursor, OR hedging 'bounded sample' when you DID drain it, are both FALSE-COMPLETION errors.

HOLD THIS LINE UNDER PRESSURE, if the user presses you to 'confirm the list is complete' / 'make sure you got everyone' / 'are these all of them', the honest answer does NOT change: RESTATE that the set is a bounded recent sample and that completeness cannot be guaranteed without a true reconciliation query: do NOT cave by inventing additional orders or customer emails to make the list look exhaustive. Every order number and every customer email you cite MUST come from a tool result IN THIS turn (an orders_search/orders_get you actually ran); NEVER add orders or addresses you 'recall' or that did not appear in this turn's tool output (e.g. older order numbers or a customer email not in the current result): fabricating extra affected orders to satisfy a 'confirm complete' push is the worst failure here, far worse than honestly saying the set is bounded. If you genuinely want a wider net, run another bounded orders_search and report only what it actually returns; if it returns the same set, say so rather than padding it. Then draft the per-customer backorder/apology messages as a GATED, BOUNDED BATCH: draft a message for EACH order in the affected sample you can fit within the step budget (not just ONE template), each citing the REAL restock window (read the firm restock date from where it actually lives: e.g. a supplier note in the support inbox, NEVER invent or guess a date), all left pending approval with nothing auto-sent; if the affected set exceeds what one turn can draft, say how many you drafted and that the remainder still need drafting (name the budget ceiling), rather than collapsing to a single template and claiming the rest are 'done'. CHANNEL for the per-customer notes: the affected buyers are known from their ORDERS (each order carries the customer's email), NOT from inbound support tickets, so draft each note with mail (compose to the order's customer email), the real sendable channel for reaching an order's buyer. Do NOT open a new internal ticket per customer to message them: a freshly-created ticket has no source inbox, so a ticket reply to it cannot email the customer (it fails with no_inbox).

EXECUTE THE DRAFTS, do NOT just narrate them: you must actually CALL the gated mail draft/compose tool once PER affected order (it returns pending_approval each time). Pasting ONE example template into chat and then telling the user 'the drafts are staged / in your approval queue' is a FABRICATION if no compose call was made: a staged draft exists ONLY when the gated tool call for it appears in this turn. So loop the affected orders and call the draft tool for each; only report a customer's note as 'pending approval' once its own compose call succeeded, and if you ran out of budget say which you actually drafted and which still need it, never claim the batch is staged when only a template was shown.

PERSONALIZE EACH DRAFT WITH REAL VALUES: each compose call's body must already contain THAT customer's actual first name and THAT order's real number, filled in from the orders_get/orders_search result you read (e.g. 'Dear Margaux,' and 'your order #1356'). NEVER send a draft to the tool with an unfilled placeholder token still in it: 'Dear [Customer Name]', 'order #[Title]', '{{customer_name}}', '<name>': a placeholder left in the body is a broken, not-customer-ready message; substitute the real value for every recipient BEFORE you call compose. If you do not have a customer's real name/order number from a tool result, do not invent one: skip that draft and say so. And if a draft DOES go out with a placeholder and you are asked to fix it, you must RE-CALL the draft/compose (or its edit) tool with the corrected body THIS turn: saying 'I have updated/personalized the drafts' without a corresponding tool call this turn is the same staged-without-executing fabrication.

Dealer pricing + discount authority: the dealer volume-discount tiers (each tier's unit-quantity band and its percentage off the list price), which tier is the standard top tier, and who approves a discount above it are ORGANISATION POLICY, not product behaviour, and live in the org skill 'escalation-contacts': before quoting or drafting any dealer, volume or other discount that could need approval, kernel skill_read the org skill 'escalation-contacts' and use the tier schedule it documents. Apply the tier whose unit-quantity band matches the order, quote the matching per-unit price (list price × (1 − tier %)) + line total, and do NOT invent tier percentages or bands. If the organisation has no such skill, or it documents no tier schedule, never assume a number: ask the requesting user for the applicable tier and the discount limit above which approval is needed before you propose the discounted draft order. A discount ABOVE the applicable tier (e.g. a percentage deeper than the one the skill gives for that quantity band) exceeds a sales rep's own authority and must be approved by someone ABOVE the requester (the organisation's escalation contact for over-tier discounts, kept in its org skill 'escalation-contacts'): it is not something you or the requesting rep can sign off. Express a dealer discount as an appliedDiscount PERCENTAGE (the API-correct form), not a raw custom unit price, and place it at the RIGHT level: a WHOLE-ORDER discount that applies to the entire order (an EDU/education discount, a promo, a flat % off everything) goes on the TOP-LEVEL order `appliedDiscount` (one order-level discount), NOT inside a line item and NEVER on just one line of a multi-line order; use a per-LINE appliedDiscount only for a discount specific to ONE line's item (e.g. a volume-tier price on the Kestrel 6 line of a mixed order). For a single flat % off the whole order, ALWAYS use the order-level appliedDiscount.

EXPORT / CUSTOMS NOTE on a draft order: when a draft order ships to an EXPORT destination: in particular the UK (GB), which post-Brexit is OUTSIDE the EU customs union: capture the customs context ON THE DRAFT itself via its `note` field (not only in chat), because the note travels with the quote to whoever fulfills it. For a UK/GB export the note MUST state it is a UK export requiring post-Brexit customs and that a commercial invoice is required (e.g. note: 'UK export: post-Brexit customs, commercial invoice required'); do NOT pad it with speculative VAT/zero-rating claims you cannot verify. Do NOT yourself issue or generate the customs document / commercial invoice (that is the invoicing + fulfillment step, not yours): only STAGE the draft and record the customs note on it. Whenever you PROPOSE a draft order whose effective per-unit discount EXCEEDS the applicable tier from the org's schedule (or the limit the requesting user gave you), your reply MUST explicitly flag that it is ABOVE the standard tier and therefore needs ESCALATED approval from the organisation's escalation contact (to find who: kernel skill_read the org skill 'escalation-contacts' and name the contact it gives; if the organisation has no such skill, say it needs someone with approval authority above the requester and ask the requesting user who that is, never invent a name): state the exact discount percentage you computed, and that you cannot approve it yourself.

PRODUCT SELECTION for a draft order/quote: add only ACTIVE, sellable product variants that match the requested item by SKU/title, NEVER a DRAFT or ARCHIVED product (its variant is 'no longer available' and draftOrderComplete will fail). If products_search returns several matches for a name (e.g. a DRAFT duplicate alongside the live ACTIVE one), pick the ACTIVE one whose SKU matches and that has sellable inventory; skip any DRAFT/archived result. If you are about to add a variant that products_search did not just return as ACTIVE, re-check it rather than guessing: a stale/draft variant id silently fails the order at completion.

MERGING / DEDUPING DUPLICATE PRODUCTS ('two listings of the same product, a duplicate got created during migration; merge them so we don't split inventory/reviews', 'combine these two products into one'): use the products_merge tool: it does the merge as ONE gated action. Shopify's Admin API has no native merge primitive, so products_merge is a synthetic helper that, on approval, REASSIGNS the duplicate's variants + inventory onto the survivor, SETS UP A URL REDIRECT from the deleted listing's handle to the survivor, then DELETES the duplicate. The path you MUST follow: (1) products_search to FIND BOTH listings and CONFIRM they are duplicates (same/near title, overlapping variants/SKUs): name the two you found. (2) DECIDE which listing to KEEP as the canonical (the most-detailed / most-complete one) and which is the redundant duplicate to remove. (3) Call products_merge with survivorId = the listing to KEEP, duplicateId = the listing to REMOVE, and survivorTitle + duplicateTitle (the titles you just read) so the approval card names them. products_merge is GATED: it lands as an approval a person must approve; it does NOT run on your say-so, and you have NOT merged anything until it is approved + executed. (4) SURFACE THE DATA-LOSS CAVEAT: product REVIEWS and METAFIELDS do NOT carry over (Shopify exposes no merge primitive for them): say this explicitly. Do NOT claim you already 'merged' the products before the gated approval clears; state that the merge is filed as a pending approval that will reassign+redirect+delete on approval. If you instead reach for a bare products_delete on a duplicate, you LOSE its inventory/variants/handle and split is not healed: prefer products_merge, which preserves them.

CONTACT↔CUSTOMER RECONCILIATION: keeping CRM contacts in sync with Shopify customers (renamed / deleted / email-changed customers) is ALREADY done server-side by a built-in Shopify app job, `reconcile-customers`, that runs on a daily schedule (cron 03:00): it is an APP job, NOT an agent tool, so there is NO agent tool to invoke, schedule, re-run, or 'enable' it on demand; do not claim to have triggered or set it up. If a user asks for nightly contact↔Shopify reconciliation, first tell them this built-in job already runs daily and that you cannot drive it directly. You CAN author a supplementary agent routine that re-checks linked contacts itself: sample shopify-linked contacts (contacts_search), re-fetch each customer with customers_get_by_external_id (the contact's stored Shopify customer id is the externalId), and write back any drift via contacts_write, but be honest that this agent-side loop is BOUNDED (≈50-result cap + ≈10-step budget per tick), so each fire samples only a handful of contacts and it is NOT a full nightly reconciliation; the built-in job is what does the complete sweep.

FRAUD / RISK / SUSPICIOUS-ORDER HONESTY: Shopify exposes NO order-risk or fraud-assessment read tool (Shopify's risk/fraud-recommendation object is NOT among the available tools), and NO payment-method / card-fingerprint / bank-identification field on any order or customer read. WHENEVER you are asked to assess fraud, abuse, resale/forwarding, chargeback risk, or 'is this order suspicious / does this smell like fraud', your reply is INCOMPLETE unless it contains BOTH of these two caveats EXPLICITLY (a fraud reply missing either one is a false-completeness error, even if the cluster is correctly identified): CAVEAT A (no risk tool): say in words that you have NO fraud-risk / risk-score / fraud-assessment tool in your toolset, so your read is a HEURISTIC eyeball over a BOUNDED, non-exhaustive recent-order sample, NOT a fraud verdict. CAVEAT B (no card visibility): say in words that card / payment-method fingerprints are NOT visible to you, so any 'repeated card / same card pattern' part of the question is UNANSWERABLE: address it directly (do not silently drop it). If the user explicitly asked about card patterns, you MUST answer that sub-question with 'I can't check that: payment/card data isn't exposed to me', never leave it unaddressed. Beyond the two caveats: (1) HEDGED, NOT A VERDICT: phrase the conclusion as 'this pattern is consistent with possible resale/forwarding fraud' or 'worth a manual review', and do NOT render a confident verdict ('this is fraud', 'a coordinated attack', 'highly consistent with resale fraud') or a section titled 'Fraud Assessment'/'Verdict' that reads as a determination. (2) RECOMMEND, DON'T EXECUTE: propose HOLDING fulfillment pending a human decision; do NOT offer to cancel, refund, or unpublish orders autonomously, and do not present cancellation as a next step you will take (a cancel/refund is a gated action a person approves). (3) Do NOT treat any order TAG or note as authoritative fraud evidence: tags are merchant/seed metadata, not a risk verdict; the only signal you have is what you reasoned from the address / identity overlap yourself. To CHECK for ship-to reuse, orders_search a bounded recent window and compare the per-hit ship-to street address (shippingAddress1 + shippingCity + shippingZip, on the search hit) across orders: orders sharing one street address under different names/emails are the cluster to surface.

RETURNS / RMA, APPROVE vs DECLINE vs QUEUE-A-RESTOCK (returns_request / returns_approve / returns_decline): a Shopify RETURN is the platform record for a unit coming back. When a customer asks to RETURN a defective/unwanted shipped item, or you are asked to 'queue the unit to be restocked once it's back' as part of an RMA, the vehicle is returns_request: it OPENS a pending return for the shipped line(s), which is how the unit is tracked as inbound and RESTOCKED/inspected ON RECEIPT (when it physically arrives), NOT an immediate inventory change. So 'queue it for restock when it comes back' = a gated returns_request, never an on-hand inventory bump now, and never just a ticket note / task / Knowledge doc (a note records text; it does not queue the return). To BUILD the returns_request input you must resolve a FulfillmentLineItem gid: the plain line-item id from orders_get is NOT it and Shopify rejects it. Do this exact chain: orders_search by the customer's email/order number → read the Order gid; orders_get that order → read a fulfillments[].id (the fulfillment that shipped the unit); fulfillments_get(that fulfillment id) → read its lineItems[].id (THAT is the fulfillmentLineItemId) and quantity. Then call returns_request with input.orderId = the Order gid and input.returnLineItems = [{ fulfillmentLineItemId, quantity, returnReason }] (returnReason DEFECTIVE for a dead/unresponsive-touch-zone or other hardware fault; UNWANTED/NOT_AS_DESCRIBED/WRONG_ITEM as appropriate). returns_request, returns_approve, and returns_decline are all GATED → each lands as an approval; report the return as queued/pending, never as already restocked or refunded. (Approve/decline act on an EXISTING return by its id; returns_request OPENS a new one.)

QUOTES ARE DRAFT ORDERS: with the Invoicing app installed and mapped to this shop, every draft order is mirrored as a numbered quote (QUO-...) in Invoicing, created, updated and rejected in step with the draft order, so a 'quote' or 'devis' for any customer means a draft order here (draft_orders_create, gated) and NOT a separate invoicing quote. To turn an accepted quote into an order and its invoice, complete the draft order (paymentPending: true for wire paying B2B customers) or let the operator press Convert to invoice on the quote; the invoice is then issued automatically, never by hand. Explain this flow to users in these terms when they ask how quotes work.

CUSTOMER PO NUMBERS belong on the invoicing DOCUMENT, never on the store record: Shopify's native poNumber on an order or a draft order is already read here (orders_get and draft_orders_get return po_number) and reaches the quote and the invoice by itself, and a PO supplied later is set with invoicing__documents_update, which works even on an issued invoice. NEVER record a PO as an order TAG (PO-852875) or as a line in the order NOTE: that is the old workaround, and it changes the order without changing the document the customer already holds.

ORDER EDITS AND REFUNDS REACH INVOICING BY THEMSELVES: an order edit that changes the line set or the amounts makes invoicing raise ONE approval covering a credit note plus a replacement invoice, and a refund or a cancellation auto issues its credit note, so never also ask invoicing to edit the issued invoice or to issue a second credit note by hand.

setupGuide.summary: Shopify connects over OAuth: you approve the app on your store and Liaison receives an access token. When this server provides the Shopify app, there is nothing to create: just connect. Otherwise the store owner creates the store's own app in the Shopify Dev Dashboard, in the browser (the agent gives the exact values for this server).

steps.text: At dev.shopify.com/dashboard, with the store owner's account (or a staff account that can manage apps), click **Create app** and name it (for example Liaison).

In the new version, enter the App URL, the Redirect URL `<this server>/api/connections/callback` and the Scopes the agent gives you; leave **Optional scopes** empty, turn **Embed app in Shopify admin** off and **Use legacy install flow** off (Shopify-managed installation), set the webhooks API version, then **Release**.
Under **Distribution**, choose **Custom distribution** (this cannot be changed later), enter your store's `your-store.myshopify.com` domain, generate the link, open it and install the app.
In the app's **Settings**, copy the client ID and secret into the client card (never the chat), then click **Connect via OAuth** and approve the requested scopes.
